data.narrative:
Corvus Robotics is a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $28.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics) valued between $1.0B and $1.6B, supplemented by a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $28.2M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $48M. Peer-median analysis of the three directly comparable companies produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with the peer set ranging from $1.0B to $1.6B. These methods produce materially different outputs, reflecting uncertainty in whether Corvus tracks toward peer performance.

The triangulated valuation range is $41M (low), $524M (median), and $1.1B (high). The wide dispersion reflects the tension between backward-looking fundraising history and forward-looking peer comparable multiples. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation relative to named peers, revenue traction, and capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort. Absent proprietary financial metrics or detailed technical due diligence, the median of $524M should be treated as indicative rather than precise.
